full_judgment:
In this Rule the petitioner has challenged a decision of the lower appellate court reversing the decision of the trial court in a pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The trial court returned the application for pre-emption to the petitioner to file it before a court with appropriate pecuniary jurisdiction. Such order of the trial court was challenged before the lower appellate court who held that the order of the trial court returning the application was bad and the pre-emption case should have been dismissed outright. Against the aforesaid order of the lower appellate court the petitioner obtained this Rule under disposal. 

 2. There was a transfer of land measuring 3.72 acres at a consideration of Taka 40 thousand. The petitioner claiming to be a contiguous owner of the land claimed the pre-emption with a part thereof measuring 0.35 acres. While making the application for the pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the petitioner deposited Taka 2 thousand alleging to be the consideration amount as contemplated under clause (b) of sub-section (3) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The trial court proceeded upon the determination of the amount that would be required to be deposited by the petitioner under clause (b) of sub-section (3) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and found that the consideration money for 0.35 acres of land shall be Taka 4,323/- instead of Taka 2 thousand as deposited earlier. The trial court having assessed the consideration money at Taka 4,323/- had to return the application to the petitioner for filing it before another court with appropriate pecuniary jurisdiction since the court concerned had no such jurisdiction to try a suit valued at above Taka 4 thousand. Consequently the application for pre-emption was ultimately filed before the First Munsif of Dacca and the balance consideration money was also deposited therein. The opposite party being the purchaser pre-emptee however challenged the earlier order of the Second Munsif of Dacca in returning the plaint and consequently an appeal was preferred before the court below. The lower appellate court found that the balance consideration amount was deposited beyond the period of statutory limitation as contemplated under sub-section (1) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the pre-emption case was liable to be dismissed as barred by limitation. The petitioner has challenged the aforesaid order of the lower appellate court in this Rule under disposal. 

 3. The only question for determination is whether the balance amount of consideration money has been deposited by the petitioner beyond 4 months from the date of the transfer of the pre-empted land and, if so, whether the petitioner was entitled to the benefit of section 14 of the Limitation Act in view of the provision of section 151 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 4. The land in question was transferred by a deed of conveyance executed on 8th April, 1974 and it was presented for registration on the aforesaid date before the appropriate sub-registry at Dacca. The pre-emption case was filed within one month from the date of the execution of the deed of conveyance in May, 1974 before the Second Munsif of Dacca. It is an admitted fact that during the pendency of the pre-emption case before the Second Munsif of Dacca the registration of the deed of conveyance was completed under section 60 of Registration Act and pursuant to section 47 of the Registration Act it took effect from the date of execution of the deed i.e. from 8th April, 1974. On 26th June, 1979 the Second Munsif of Dacca having proceeded to determine the final amount to be deposited by the petitioner found that the consideration amount in question would be Taka 4,323/- which was beyond the jurisdiction of the Second Munsif of Dacca and consequently the application of pre-emption case was returned to the petitioner who duly filed the same before the First Munsif of Dacca having pecuniary jurisdiction to entertain the case on 15th July, 1976 and also deposited the balance consideration money of Taka 2,323/- in addition to Taka 2,000/- already deposited earlier. It appears that upto 26th June, 1972 the petitioner was pursuing the pre-emption case before a wrong forum which lacked the appropriate pecuniary jurisdiction. The question is whether time from the date of the filing of the pre-emption case in May, 1974 before the Second Munsif of Dacca till the returning of the application on 26th June, 1976 would be computed and excluded under Section 14 of the Limitation Act read with section 151(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In this connection it may be observed that if section 14 of Limitation Act is made applicable in the present case and if the entire period of the pre-emption case remaining pending before the Second Munsif of Dacca is taken into consideration for the purpose of exclusion from the period of limitation in that event the deposit of balance consideration money on 15th, July, 1976 is well within the statutory period of 4 months from the date of the transfer of the land under pre-emption. Coming into the application of section 14 of the Limitation Act in a pre-emption case reference may be made to section 151 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Sub-section (1) of Section 151 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act says that excepting sections 6, 7, 8, 9 & 29 of the Limitation Act the remaining provisions of the Limitation Act shall apply to all suits, appeals and applications arising under part V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Admittedly section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act being in Chapter XIII is included within Part V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In such circumstances, it is quite clear that section 14 of the Limitation Act is applicable to an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Sub-section (2) of section 151 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act however has stated that all suits, appeals and applications referred to in Part V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act shall be instituted within the time prescribed therein and any such suit, appeal and application made after prescribed period of limitation shall be dismissed. This provision merely reiterates the application of such limitation in such Act without any reference to the period of limitation provided in the Limitation Act. 

 5. This provision of sub-section (2) of Section 151 shall however be read subject to sub-section (1) of section 151 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act wherein section 14 of Limitation Act is made applicable to an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So far as the section 14 of Limitation Act is concerned once it has been found that a party was delinquently pursuing a matter before another court such period shall be computed and excluded from the period of limitation. Thus, it is quite clear that the period when the pre-emption case remains pending before the Second Munsif of Dacca till the order returning the application for filing before another court with appropriate pecuniary jurisdiction shall be excluded for the purpose of computing the period of limitation under section 14 of the Limitation Act. That being done evidently the deposit of the balance consideration money made before the First Munsif of Dacca on the date of the filing of the application for pre-emption on 15th July, 1976 was done within 4 months from the date of the transfer of the impugned land claimed under pre-emption. In such circumstances deposit made can not be held to have been done beyond the period of limitation and the pre-emption application can not be dismissed on that account and consequently the order of the Second Munsif of Dacca made on 26.6.76 by order No. 27 in Miscellaneous Case No. 114 of 1974 returning the application for pre-emption can not be said to be not in according with law.
